Theorem
[Energy estimates] ↗ thm:symmetric-hyperbolic-approximate-solutions 1. ch7:7.3-thm-2\group Energy Estimates

There exists a constant $C$, depending only on $n$ and the coefficients, such that \[ \max _{0 \leq t \leq T} \| u^\epsilon (t)\| _{H^1(\mathbb {R}^n;\mathbb {R}^m)} + \| u_t^\epsilon \| _{L^2(0,T;L^2(\mathbb {R}^n;\mathbb {R}^m))} \] \[ \leq C(\| g\| _{H^1(\mathbb {R}^n;\mathbb {R}^m)} + \| f\| _{L^2(0,T;H^1(\mathbb {R}^n;\mathbb {R}^m))} + \| f'\| _{L^2(0,T;L^2(\mathbb {R}^n;\mathbb {R}^m))}) \tag {17} \] for each $0 < \epsilon \leq 1$.

Proof

\sketch Take the Euclidean inner product with $u^{\varepsilon }$ and integrate over space. Symmetry permits integration by parts of the principal matrices, the viscosity term is dissipative, and bounded lower-order terms are controlled by Gronwall uniformly in $\varepsilon $.

□
